newsitem.title: INDIA: Prospects of political stability lift Delhi shares.
newsitem.headline: Prospects of political stability lift Delhi shares.

text.p: Shares on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed higher in brisk trade on Tuesday, boosted by prospects of an end to prevailing political instability, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 7.58 points higher at 760.63.
"Though markets displayed some signs of recovery, any decisive trend would emerge only after the forming of the next government," said Suresh Aggarwal of brokers Jai Mata Securities.
Brokers say they expect the United Front coalition to form a government with the Congress party's support next week, ending weeks of uncertainty surrounding the country's political future.
Traders said they expected shares prices to react favourably to the passage of the budget for 1997/98 (April-March), due to be taken up by parliament in a three-day session beginning April 21.
"I think budget is all that the market is concerned about," said one broker.
Reliance Industries moved both ways on alternate bouts of buying and selling by speculators before settling 2.75 rupees higher at 267.75, brokers said.
State Bank of India closed 14.00 rupees higher at 286.00.
